summary: Discovery focused on Redwood quickstart and PLG self-serve flow. Emberlynx wants a low-friction path to time-to-first-token, evaluate hosted API with free credits, and understand path to Dedicated or Private for security/compliance. Key concerns: data residency, KMS integration, latency/cost tradeoffs. Next steps: pricing + quickstart materials, benchmark template, security deep-dive.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Quick intros?
[00:10] Alicia (Emberlynx CTO): Hey, Alicia here, CTO at Emberlynx. We build an analytics platform and are exploring LLM features.
[00:15] Ben (Lead ML Eng): Ben, I run ML infra. We're evaluating self-serve APIs and options for dedicated/private later.
[00:25] Sean (Redwood SE): Sean here, I focus on latency and deployment patterns. Happy to walk through performance and PoC setups.
[00:35] Maya: Great. Goal for today is to understand your current stack, what quickstart looks like, and next steps to run a small PoC.
[00:45] Alicia: High level — want a low-friction way to try Redwood hosted API, see how fast we can get first token, and then assess if we need Dedicated or Private for compliance.
[00:55] Ben: Right, time-to-first-token is important — developer experience. We also care about unit cost and tail latency at ~512 tokens.
[01:10] Sean: Totally. Our PLG quickstart is typically: sign up, free credits, API key, sample prompt, and SDK examples. You can get a token in minutes. For benchmarking we provide a small harness.
[01:30] Ben: How do the free credits work? Any limits on model selection?
[01:40] Maya: Free credits are platform credits tied to the account; they cover most curated open models and Redwood-verified variants. For large models we sometimes restrict bigger capacity until we know expected usage, but you can test locally.
[01:55] Alicia: And can we run the quickstart in our VPC or is it only hosted?
[02:05] Sean: Quickstart is hosted. For Private deployments we have a separate onboarding — but the hosted API gives you a quick path to validate functionality. If it looks good, we can discuss Dedicated capacity or Private (VPC/on-prem) and KMS integrations.
[02:25] Alicia: Samira from security here — quick question on logs and PII. If a user sends PII, is that retained?
[02:35] Samira (Security): Yeah I'm Samira — need to confirm retention, audit logs, and encryption at rest.
[02:45] Maya: We have options: hosted default retention policy, plus Dedicated/Private where you can control retention and KMS. We'll share the SOC2 docs and retention SLA.
[02:55] Ben: Latency-wise, how do you compare hosted vs dedicated? We need 95th percentile under 400ms for small requests.
[03:10] Sean: For short sequences and curated models, hosted can meet <300ms in many regions. Dedicated gives you guaranteed throughput and more predictable tail latency. We also use KV-cache and batching optimizations — though that can be tuned per workload.
[03:35] Ben: KV cache? Did you say K-V cache?
[03:40] Sean: Yeah K-V cache, key-value cache — apologies. It stores prefixes to speed generation.
[03:50] Alicia: What about model variants and quantization? If we care about cost we might want quantized models.
[03:58] Sean: We recommend certain quantization profiles based on sequence lengths; Redwood Optimize suggests tradeoffs. We'll propose a config for your workload.
[04:10] Ben: For PoC, what does the benchmark look like? We want to test time-to-first-token, throughput, and cost per 1M tokens.
[04:20] Maya: Sean will share a benchmark template — small harness that runs synthetic prompts at 1, 16, 32 batch sizes and records p50/p95 and token costs.
[04:35] Sean: I'll include curl examples and the SDK, and a pre-populated script that hits the hosted endpoint using free-credit account.
[04:45] Samira: On compliance, we need to know about KMS/HSM support and whether you support customer-managed keys in Private/Dedicated.
[04:55] Maya: Customer-managed KMS is available for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we offer encryption at rest but not customer-managed KMS by default.
[05:05] Alicia: Data residency — can we keep data in EU? We're based in EU and have EU customers.
[05:15] Sean: Yes, we have regions — hosted EU region and Private deployments can be in your region. We'll flag data residency in the SOW for Private.
[05:25] Ben: One concern is egress costs and model updates. If you route to fallback models, will that affect cost predictability?
[05:35] Maya: We have routing policies — you can pin model versions to control cost. Fallbacks are opt-in and controlled via rollout policies.
[05:45] Ben: Ok. Walk me through the sign-up quickstart steps — what's the bare minimum to hit the API?
[05:55] Sean: Sign-up, create API key, run SDK example, call the /generate endpoint with a small prompt. We'll include a Postman collection and Node/Python examples. Usually developers get tokens in <10 minutes.
[06:10] Alicia: Are there quotas for the free credits? Any rate limits?
[06:20] Maya: Free credits have daily caps to prevent abuse, but adequate for PoC. Rate limits are per account but we can temporarily raise them for trial.
[06:30] Ben: For ML infra, we want to test latency from our EU region and from our US cluster. Do you provide region-specific endpoints?
[06:45] Sean: There's region-aware endpoints. We'll give you regional URLs for EU and US.
[06:55] Samira: For the security deep-dive, we'll need encryption diagrams, SOC2 attestation, SSO/SAML integration details.
[07:05] Maya: We'll attach our security pack and SAML doc. Also include a network diagram for Private.
[07:15] Ben: If the hosted API looks good, what's the lead time to Dedicated?
[07:25] Maya: Dedicated can take weeks depending on capacity and contract; typical is 2-6 weeks. Private on-prem is longer — depends on procurement and infra readiness.
[07:40] Alicia: We're also comparing against Anthropic and OpenAI. Any differentiation we should call out?
[07:50] Maya: Redwood is focused on production economics and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. We emphasize observability and cost controls like batching/cache and rollout policies to avoid surprises.
[08:05] Ben: Do you provide cost estimates for specific throughput?
[08:12] Sean: Yes, we'll model token costs given batch sizes and requests per second; include amortized infra costs for Dedicated.
[08:20] Alicia: For the PoC, what success criteria should we set?
[08:30] Ben: I'd say: 1) time-to-first-token < 150ms in EU region for small prompts, 2) p95 latency < 400ms, 3) cost per 1M tokens below threshold X (we'll provide a target), and 4) security controls validated.
[08:50] Maya: Sounds good. We'll align the benchmark with those criteria.
[09:00] Sean: Quick note — sometimes transcription or small dev misconceptions, but the test harness will measure end-to-end.
[09:10] Alicia: Are there SDKs for our stack? We use Python and Node, and have some Go infra.
[09:20] Maya: SDKs for Python/Node are first-class; Go community SDK exists. We'll share code snippets.
[09:28] Ben: About model catalog — can we bring our own model or only Redwood curated ones?
[09:35] Sean: For hosted we usually run curated models; Dedicated/Private allow bringing your own model artifacts. We can discuss model onboarding.
[09:45] Samira: If we go Dedicated, do you do penetration tests or provide SOC attestations for us to include in our vendor review?
[09:55] Maya: Yes, we can provide SOC2 Type II and pen test summaries. We'll include the attestation PDF in the security pack.
[10:05] Alicia: Ok let's talk timeline — we want to spin up quickstart next week and run a short PoC inside 2 weeks.
[10:15] Maya: That works. I'll send the quickstart guide and grant free credits. Sean will share the benchmark harness.
[10:25] Ben: One operational question: does Redwood keep prompts in logs for debugging? How granular are audit logs?
[10:35] Sean: We have configurable audit logs, default redaction is available. For Dedicated/Private you can control retention and full audit logging.
[10:45] Samira: Please also include SSO mapping and RBAC examples.
[10:55] Maya: Will do.
[11:05] Alicia: On pricing, can you give ballpark ranges for hosted vs Dedicated?
[11:15] Maya: Hosted is pay-as-you-go token pricing; Dedicated is committed capacity with lower unit costs. I'll include ballpark numbers in the follow-up.
[11:25] Ben: For benchmarking, please include guidance on sequence length distribution — our workload is often ~256 tokens.
[11:35] Sean: Noted. We'll tailor the harness to 256 tokens primarily and include 64/512 as edge cases.
[11:45] Alicia: Any gotchas about rate limiting with SDKs?
[11:55] Sean: SDKs implement exponential backoff. We'll include retry best practices and guidance for batching.
[12:05] Maya: Quick recap: we'll send quickstart + free credits, security pack, pricing, benchmark harness. Emberlynx will: run quickstart, provide target cost threshold and schedule security deep-dive.
[12:20] Ben: Sounds good.
[12:25] Alicia: One more — will we be able to test model updates and rollbacks in the PoC?
[12:35] Sean: Yes, rollouts and pinning are available; we can demo canary and rollback features in the Console.
[12:45] Samira: Ok schedule the security session with our procurement and legal too.
[12:55] Maya: I'll coordinate. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with materials.
[13:05] [meeting ends]

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-parses (K-V vs KV cache, Redwood product names sometimes abbreviated). Links shared during call: /docs/quickstart (quickstart guide), /security/soc2.pdf (security pack), shared: benchmark-template.zip (will be emailed).
